title: Vesper and the Bridge
premise: In the river city of Vesper, mapmaker's apprentice Dominic Nakamura inherits an unfinished atlas her master died protecting—a survey of the great bridge that the ruling council has ordered closed and quietly condemned. As winter seals the bridge and the workshop's eviction looms, Dominic discovers her master's final plates hide evidence that the closure was engineered to erase a district's history and displace its people. Racing flood season and council spies, she completes the atlas as both memorial and indictment; in the end she surrenders the original to save the bridge-keepers from arrest, but smuggled copies force the city to reckon with what it tried to bury.
about_author: X. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing municipal maps of drowned and demolished neighborhoods. Vesper and the Bridge is their second novel, following the acclaimed The Cartographer's Debt.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In the weeks after Master Ivo's funeral, Dominic works alone in the drafty workshop, inking the atlas's final plate while creditors circle. She finds his hidden notes about the bridge survey—measurements no one commissioned. Emotional beat: grief hardening into purpose; she decides to finish the work he died for.

chapters.title: Winter Seals the Span
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The council closes the bridge for the season earlier than any year on record, stranding the ferry-district families who depend on it. Delivering proofs across town, Dominic witnesses the closure up close when a gate guard seizes her satchel of drawings. Emotional beat: unease—the closure feels less like weather than strategy.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sela's POV (a bridge-keeper's daughter). Sela ferries stranded workers by skiff and recruits Dominic to chart safe ice routes, offering in exchange the oral histories Ivo never wrote down. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two keepers of memory—one in ink, one in voice—recognize each other.

chapters.title: What the Survey Shows
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Comparing Ivo's plates against official records, Dominic proves the bridge was declared unsafe using falsified stress figures—and that the 'condemned' district sits atop land the council's patrons covet. Emotional beat: dread and resolve entwined; knowledge becomes dangerous.

chapters.title: A Visit from the Council
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Surveyor-General Brandt visits the workshop, courteous and chilling, offering to buy Ivo's unfinished atlas outright. Dominic lies smoothly for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into performance; she understands the workshop is now a target.

chapters.title: Copying by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Sela organizes the ferry families to hand-copy key plates overnight while Dominic perfects the master atlas. A raid scare nearly exposes them; an old keeper burns his own copy rather than risk the others. Emotional beat: solidarity and sacrifice—the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Eviction
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Bailiffs seal the workshop with Ivo's library inside; Dominic escapes through the coal chute carrying only the finished atlas and one hidden plate. Sela hides her among the bridge pilings. Emotional beat: loss and displacement—she has become one of the erased.

chapters.title: Flood Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With thaw floods rising, the council's neglect of the bridge endangers the very district they displaced; Sela's father refuses to abandon his post at the gates. Dominic must choose between fleeing with the atlas or staying to document the crisis. Emotional beat: duty versus survival at full pressure.

chapters.title: The Bridge Holds
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. During the flood peak, Dominic publicly presents the atlas on the bridge itself, reading Ivo's figures aloud as the span holds under weight the council called fatal. Brandt orders her arrested; the crowd of keepers and ferrymen stands between. Emotional beat: truth as confrontation—love of place against power.

chapters.title: Vesper, Corrected
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, the copied atlas circulates openly; an inquiry reopens the bridge, though Ivo's name stays officially uncleared. Dominic begins a new map—not of streets, but of everything the city chose to forget. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; memory survives at cost, and the work continues.
